records.summary: A GitHub Actions 90-day usage export records 1,966,401 self-hosted macOS runner-minutes, averaging 21,848.9 minutes/day. Pricing every minute at only WarpBuild's cheapest documented macOS rate yields a $52,437.36 per 30-day-month replacement-cost floor.

evidence.label: Scrapbook 90-day Actions usage source
evidence.basis: Derived directly from the GitHub Actions 90-day usage CSV downloaded on 2026-09-23; the checked-in source summary preserves aggregate minutes and the leading macOS workflows.

claims.population: All rows in the export where runner type is self-hosted and runtime OS is macOS
claims.note: The export contains 1,966,401 self-hosted macOS minutes. ci.yml alone accounts for 1,345,657 minutes, or about 68.4 percent of this total.

claims.population: Self-hosted macOS Actions workload
claims.note: This 90-day average is about 16.8 percent above the separate 18,704-minute one-day accounting from September 22.

claims.population: All 1,966,401 self-hosted macOS minutes priced at WarpBuild's cheapest documented 6-vCPU macOS rate
claims.note: Floor valuation only: 655,467 equivalent minutes per 30 days at $0.08/min. No 12-vCPU premium is applied. This is replacement-cost exposure, not a claim that every minute was actually billed to Warp or saved by one contributor.

claims.measurementWindow: Same 90-day Actions export annualized over 365 days
claims.population: Same self-hosted macOS workload priced at $0.08/min
claims.note: Annualized replacement-cost floor at the 90-day average. Any 12-vCPU Warp usage would raise the equivalent value.

claims.population: Nine CMUX workflows scheduling macOS jobs; only time that actually held a runner
claims.note: This independent issue-level accounting remains a useful corroborating snapshot but is no longer the primary economic baseline.

records.title: Compile the E2E test product once and reuse it on reruns
records.summary: Split the focused E2E dispatch into filter, build, and test jobs so invalid selectors fail on Linux before a Mac starts and reruns download the retained test product instead of recompiling it.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13908
evidence.basis: The PR body measures 60 dispatches, isolates the approximately 15.3-minute compile portion, and states that reruns now download the product and compile nothing.

claims.population: Reruns of a failed focused E2E dispatch while the retained product remains available
claims.note: Fresh dispatches do not claim lower total runner minutes; this figure is the measured compile portion removed from a rerun by the new job split.

records.title: Report recorded failures even when app-host results are incomplete
records.summary: Fixed an early-return path where one missing terminal test result caused the shard to suppress every failure it had successfully recorded, leaving red full-suite runs without the names of the tests that regressed.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13962
evidence.basis: The PR body compares CI output with the same run's logs and records 60 XCTest assertion failures plus 88 Swift Testing failures that produced zero ratchet lines.

claims.population: Recorded XCTest and Swift Testing failures in the incomplete app-host shards
claims.note: The fix changes diagnostics, not the fail-closed verdict: incomplete runs remain failed while recorded failures are now named.

records.title: Cached-diagnostics replay crash with mixed prefix-mapped inputs
records.summary: Reduced a real compilation-cache crash to three Swift source files and one resource, traced the replay failure through CachedDiagnostics and FileSpecificDiagnosticConsumer, decoded the CAS diagnostics blob, and connected the missing-file condition to an earlier prefix-map fix.

evidence.label: Swift issue 92545
evidence.basis: The issue contains the deterministic reproducer, controls, decoded cache evidence, stack trace, suspected failure path, workarounds, and related prior fixes.

records.title: Seed the test compilation cache from one clean build
records.summary: Stopped the test compilation-cache seeder from restoring its previous seed by prefix and recursively accumulating old generations until it crossed the save bound and froze.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13797
evidence.basis: The PR body records cache growth across scheduled seeds, the 5 GiB save bound, one clean-build result, producer timings, and the per-pull-request download consequence.

claims.population: pull requests restoring the shared test compilation-cache seed
claims.note: The clean seed is about 3.5 GiB instead of roughly 5.0 GiB, so every pull request restores about 1.5 GiB less.

records.title: Debounce macOS admission on superseded pull-request pushes
records.summary: Inserted a bounded Linux admission delay before expensive macOS work so rapid follow-up pushes cancel stale runs before a Mac starts, then replayed a day of job timings to estimate the avoided work and latency trade-off.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13644
evidence.basis: The PR body contains the 24-hour run sample, cancelled-minute breakdown, replay method, and delay trade-off table.

claims.population: Superseded pull-request runs that would otherwise start macOS work
claims.note: Replay estimate at the default 180-second delay; the same analysis measured a 1.4-minute median increase to the green signal.

records.title: Route pull-request macOS jobs to sponsored capacity
records.summary: Measured a day of macOS workload by triggering event, then routed the pull-request burst lane from paid overflow onto sponsored Blacksmith capacity while leaving other events on the existing repository variable.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13658
evidence.basis: The PR body records the 24-hour workload measurement, event split, routing change, and rollback control.

claims.population: Pull-request macOS overflow work in the sampled CMUX CI day
claims.note: This moves workload onto sponsored capacity; it does not claim the compute disappeared.

records.title: Trigger the persistent Mac router once per CI run
records.summary: Changed the persistent-Mac router from a workflow activity emitted for every CI job to the once-per-run requested event, eliminating thousands of duplicate router invocations while preserving the trust boundary and hosted fallback.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13645
evidence.basis: The PR body records the 24-hour router-run counts, explains why the old activity fired per job, and documents the re-run coverage trade-off.

claims.population: persistent-macos-router workflow invocations
claims.note: The measured baseline was about 6,864 router runs/day; the once-per-CI-run trigger was expected to produce about 1,253/day, an 82% reduction.

records.title: Seed compilation cache on the runner pull requests restore from
records.summary: Found that the nightly compilation-cache seed and pull-request consumer ran on different runner layouts even though the cache fingerprint included the workspace path, making the seed impossible to restore by construction.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13754
evidence.basis: The PR body records the exact cache miss, runner labels, fingerprint mechanism, and a measured 19.9-minute cold compile step.

claims.population: Pull-request admission before the cache producer and consumer runner layouts matched
claims.note: The PR explicitly left warm compile time unmeasured until the next scheduled seed.

records.title: Move Computer Use runtime out of the 3,700-file app module
records.summary: Moved the Computer Use runtime into a local package and a shared process-identity type into CmuxFoundation so edits in those files stop paying the app target's whole-module planning and compilation cost.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13132
evidence.basis: The PR body records warm incremental comment-only edits before and after the move, app-target file counts, package tests, and the limit imposed by public-interface changes.

claims.population: comment-only edit to AgentPIDProcessIdentity.swift before and after moving it from the app target to CmuxFoundation
claims.note: The measured build fell from 38.9 seconds to 13.3 seconds and compiled zero app-target Swift files after the move.

records.title: Reuse one warm DerivedData across development tags
records.summary: Changed tagged development builds from one fresh DerivedData tree per tag to a reusable warm tree, while keeping build serialization, CLI lookup, path validation, and cleanup ownership explicit.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13131
evidence.basis: The PR records a same-machine matrix covering fresh DerivedData, same-commit tag reuse, branch/tag switches, small edits, larger app edits, and interface-invalidating changes.

claims.population: new development tag at the same commit after a warm build
claims.note: Fresh DerivedData took 953 seconds; a new tag using the already-warm shared DerivedData took 35.7 seconds.

records.title: Stop pull requests from evicting shared cache seeds
records.summary: Found that pull-request jobs were writing gigabyte-scale, PR-scoped cache entries that other pull requests could never read, rapidly evicting the main-branch seeds and forcing expensive macOS builds cold.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13160
evidence.basis: The PR body records the cache inventory, entry scope, cold build timings, cache-store limits, and the change to restore-only pull-request consumers.

claims.population: 27 GitHub cache entries visible to the repository
claims.note: The oldest macOS entry was only five minutes old and the shared Debug compilation seed was already missing. Pull-request jobs had 14 save+restore cache steps and wrote 1–3 GB PR-scoped entries.

records.title: Seed the Debug compilation cache from main
records.summary: Added a scheduled main-branch seed for the Debug compilation cache so pull-request compile admission could restore shared package work instead of always beginning from an empty cache.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13060
evidence.basis: The PR body records the cold admission baseline, module timing breakdown, cache policy, local experiments, and the distinction between measured and expected CI behavior.

claims.population: macOS compile admission from an empty compilation cache
claims.note: The PR deliberately did not quote an unmeasured CI savings number before the scheduled seed had run.

records.title: Parallelize slow and history-dependent CI guards
records.summary: Split one roughly 390-second guard job into shallow, history-only, CLI-script, and source-lint jobs so independent policy checks run concurrently before macOS admission.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 13378 follow-up measurement
evidence.basis: The follow-up reusable-workflow PR records the accepted before/after measurement for PR 13097: 385.5 seconds to 124.3 seconds on the guard critical path, with Linux runner-minutes increasing from 6.43 to 7.49.

claims.population: Linux guard path gating macOS admission
claims.note: Measured guard wall time fell from 385.5 seconds to 124.3 seconds, about a 68% reduction.

claims.population: Linux guard jobs
claims.note: Runner consumption rose from 6.43 to 7.49 minutes because parallel jobs duplicate setup work. The change intentionally spends cheap compute to return the macOS admission answer sooner.
